steps.tx: A chronic, systemic venereal infection caused by the fastidious, tightly coiled spirochaete Treponema pallidum subspecies pallidum is **syphilis**. Transmitted primarily through direct contact with active infectious mucosal lesions during sexual intercourse, the disease progresses sequentially through primary, secondary, latent, and tertiary clinical stages if left untreated.
steps.say: A chronic systemic venereal infection caused by the spirochaete Treponema pallidum is syphilis. Transmitted through sexual contact with active mucosal lesions, the disease progresses through primary, secondary, latent, and tertiary stages if untreated.

steps.tx: The pathognomonic physical manifestation of primary syphilis appearing at the inoculation site after an incubation period of ten to ninety days is a hard **chancre**. Beginning as a painless indurated papule that rapidly erodes into a clean-based, painless, highly infectious ulcer with raised cartilaginous margins, it is accompanied by non-tender, rubbery regional lymphadenopathy.
steps.say: The pathognomonic physical manifestation of primary syphilis appearing after three weeks is a hard chancre. Beginning as a painless indurated papule that erodes into a clean-based painless ulcer with cartilaginous edges, it is accompanied by non-tender regional lymphadenopathy.

left.title: Syphilitic Hard Chancre
points: Single, painless ulcer with indurated, clean base

right.title: Chancroid Soft Chancre
points: Treated with single-dose Azithromycin or Ceftriaxone

steps.tx: Systemic haematogenous dissemination occurring four to ten weeks after the primary chancre manifests as **secondary syphilis**. The clinical hallmark is a symmetrical, non-pruritic maculopapular or copper-penny papulosquamous rash prominently involving the palms and soles, accompanied by generalized lymphadenopathy, mucous patches in the mouth, and moth-eaten alopecia.
steps.say: Systemic dissemination occurring weeks after the primary chancre manifests as secondary syphilis. The clinical hallmark is a symmetrical copper-penny rash prominently involving the palms and soles, accompanied by generalized lymphadenopathy, oral mucous patches, and moth-eaten alopecia.

vis.alt: Clinical appearance of palmoplantar rash and mucous lesions in secondary syphilis.
vis.caption: Symmetrical palmoplantar papulosquamous eruption in secondary syphilis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: In warm, intertriginous anatomical folds such as the perineum, perianal region, and vulva, hypertrophic coalescent secondary syphilitic papules form broad, flat, moist, greyish-white plaques designated as **condylomata lata**. Teeming with motile spirochaetes visible on darkfield microscopy, condylomata lata represent one of the most infectious cutaneous manifestations of treponemal disease.
steps.say: In warm intertriginous skin folds like the perineum and vulva, secondary syphilitic papules form broad moist plaques designated as condylomata lata. Teeming with motile spirochaetes on darkfield microscopy, they are highly infectious.

left.title: Condylomata Lata (Syphilis)
points: Broad, flat-topped, smooth moist grey plaques

right.title: Condylomata Acuminata (Warts)
points: Treated with cryotherapy, podophyllin, or ablation

steps.tx: Serological diagnosis requires combining non-treponemal and treponemal tests. Non-treponemal tests (VDRL, RPR) detect anticardiolipin antibodies; titers fluctuate dynamically with disease activity, serving as the gold standard for monitoring therapeutic cure. Specific treponemal tests (**TPHA**, FTA-ABS) detect antibodies directed against treponemal antigens, remaining reactive for life regardless of treatment.
steps.say: Serological diagnosis requires combining non-treponemal and treponemal tests. Non-treponemal tests like VDRL detect anticardiolipin antibodies, fluctuating with disease activity to monitor cure. Specific treponemal tests like TPHA detect antitreponemal antibodies, remaining positive for life.

rows: Titer reflects disease activity; 4-fold decline indicates cure
High specificity (> 99%); remains positive for life
Caused by pregnancy, antiphospholipid syndrome, leprosy, malaria

steps.tx: The absolute treatment of choice across all clinical stages of syphilis is parenteral penicillin G. Early syphilis (primary, secondary, and early latent under one year) responds to a single intramuscular injection of long-acting **benzathine penicillin** G (2.4 million units). Late latent syphilis and cardiovascular tertiary syphilis require three weekly doses of 2.4 million units.
steps.say: The absolute treatment of choice across all stages of syphilis is parenteral penicillin G. Early syphilis responds to a single intramuscular injection of long-acting benzathine penicillin G at 2.4 million units. Late latent and tertiary syphilis require three weekly doses.

Oral Doxycycline 100 mg bid for 28 days
Aqueous Crystalline Penicillin G 18-24 MU/day IV for 10-14 days

steps.tx: An acute, self-limiting systemic febrile reaction developing within two to twenty-four hours after initiating penicillin in secondary syphilis is the **Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction**. Driven by sudden massive spirochaetal lysis releasing endotoxin-like lipoproteins, patients develop transient fevers, chills, tachycardia, and flushing, managed with reassurance and antipyretics without stopping penicillin.
steps.say: An acute febrile reaction developing within twenty-four hours after starting penicillin in secondary syphilis is the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction. Driven by sudden spirochaetal lysis releasing endotoxins, patients experience fever, chills, and flushing, managed with reassurance and paracetamol without stopping antibiotics.

steps.tx: In resource-constrained settings, sexually transmitted infections are managed through evidence-based **syndromic management**. Patients presenting with urethral discharge receive dual empiric therapy covering both Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis (intramuscular ceftriaxone 500 mg plus oral azithromycin or doxycycline), while genital ulcers are treated empirically for both primary syphilis and chancroid.
steps.say: In clinical practice, sexually transmitted infections are managed through evidence-based syndromic management. Patients presenting with urethral discharge receive dual empiric therapy covering gonorrhoea and chlamydia with ceftriaxone and azithromycin, while genital ulcers are treated for syphilis and chancroid.

Oral Acyclovir 400 mg tid for 7 to 10 days
